top_issues.issue: Fissures do not light their surrounding stone
top_issues.why: Ref 04's main idea is fissures washing the rock around them. Here the glow stays on the line itself.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a soft emissive falloff or local light tint onto the host tile and its neighbours, keeping the dark between fissure clusters.

top_issues.issue: Repeating diagonal-split tile pattern
top_issues.why: Every tile has the same triangle split, so the rock reads as a stamped grid rather than a broken faceted mass like 03.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Vary facet orientation, inset and slight per-tile height or normal jitter so neighbouring cubes break the grid.

top_issues.issue: Beam-lit faces wash to white or grey and lose the world hue
top_issues.why: One hue per world should survive in the lit areas; pale cream or grey walls weaken the amber and sea-green identity.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep the albedo tint saturated under the lamp, or tint the specular and highlight toward the world hue.

top_issues.issue: No nacre or iridescence on MAELIS rock
top_issues.why: Ref 06 is pearlescent sea-green; the game's version is plain grey-green.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a subtle view- or facet-dependent hue shift (green to violet sheen) on the MAELIS rock faces only.

top_issues.issue: Back-wall and unlit rock are flat grids
top_issues.why: The rock mass away from the light has little form, so depth separation relies on the beam alone.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give the back wall a cooler, hazier, recessed value than the foreground rock, with faint facet variation.

top_issues.issue: Solid fill masses read as flat brown slabs, and the crack trim is busy

per_shot.note: Wordmark sits over the lit surface base. Sign boards (FUE, TRADE) show through and between the letters, so the logo competes with the scene and there's no sense of descent.
Clean, sparse HUD in the corners (fuel/hull bars, depth, lumens, cargo). Readable against the dusk and stays out of the way.

Strong spaced OUT wordmark, but the background is flat cool grey and the text lines are wide (~620px), so it reads plain, not sacred or quiet.

top_issues.issue: Title wordmark is laid over the busiest part of the scene
top_issues.why: Signs and buildings break up the letters and the tagline/button float over clutter. It misses the 01-title mood: a dark shaft, warmth rising from below, one small lit pod.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Frame the camera so the surface base sits high and the wordmark and menu sit over dark rock, with warmth rising from the bottom of the frame.

top_issues.issue: Modal panels use a cool navy palette that doesn't match the world
top_issues.why: The brief says one hue per world (VEIL amber). The panel reads as a stock UI card, not part of the lit-from-within world.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Warm near-black panel with a thin bronze or amber edge, keeping the existing type hierarchy.

top_issues.issue: Ending page has no light
top_issues.why: The story is about light, but the end screen is a flat grey void with no glow, so the emotional beat falls flat.
top_issues.suggested_direction: A soft warm bloom behind the wordmark, and a narrower text measure for the body.

top_issues.issue: Emissive glow is clipped to the tile square
top_issues.why: The glow reads as a lit square cell rather than soft bloom into the dark, which goes against 'Glow' and makes ores look like UI tiles
top_issues.suggested_direction: Use a radial falloff halo that is not bounded by the cell, and dim the cell-wide fill so the ore shape carries the read

top_issues.issue: Overexposed gem surfaces wash out colour identity
top_issues.why: Voidopal and mimic go white-pink and copper's teal goes mint-white, so the hue tells that distinguish them are lost
top_issues.suggested_direction: Cap emissive and specular so facets keep saturated blue/violet/magenta and verdigris teal; let the halo carry brightness

top_issues.issue: Nacre shape language is wrong
top_issues.why: It is a spiky crystal rosette, which competes with frostbloom, silver and diamond instead of reading as a ribbed shell or fan
top_issues.suggested_direction: Build a scalloped fan or shell from stacked curved ridges on a slate chip, and keep the pearly pink-teal sheen soft

top_issues.issue: Gold is lemon and sandwiched rather than split open

top_issues.suggested_direction: Shift toward amber-gold, and make it one rock with a broken face exposing glowing gold

top_issues.issue: Copper crust too pale
top_issues.why: Teal crust plus orange cells is copper's only tell, and a mint-white crust weakens it
top_issues.suggested_direction: Use a darker, more saturated verdigris base with less specular

top_issues.issue: Gold is a sandwich, not a split boulder

top_issues.issue: Halos are oversized and rounded-square on some ores
top_issues.why: A large halo flattens the ore into a lit tile and reduces how much light seems to land on the surrounding rock
top_issues.suggested_direction: Use a tighter, truly radial falloff, and add some spill onto neighbouring rock faces

minerals.why: B's radial halos and controlled exposure preserve each ore's colour identity (copper teal, voidopal facets, mimic opal) and bloom into the dark as briefed, where A clips glow to square tiles and blows gems out to white. B's only regression is iron getting lost on the darker rock.
